title: callData: the disabled-package refusal of a relation condition stops at the first hop (and the no-protocol fallback still serves the addressed object)
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC

Follow-up from #35526 (PR #36337, the member-caller half). Found by the L2 record 7077187908 on PR #36337, which graded S1 and S2 non-blocking and carried here, plus escalation E3. Filed by the seat. Parent: #35526.

## What happens

1. **The refusal is one hop deep (S1, read, not measured).** `refuseUnservedRelationTargets` walks the queried object's relation sites once and does not descend. The engine serves nested relation conditions up to three hops (`RELATION_CONDITION_MAX_HOPS = 3`, #33626), and its reads ask no disabled-package question. The data route asks at every hop. So `aggregate dp_alpha where { c_ref: { b2_ref: { secret_note: VALUE } } }`, with C enabled and B disabled, should still answer 1 / 0 to a member through `callData`. The one-hop walk dates from #22823, so the same gap holds for the exposure question, and by the same reading for the stdio bridge's `enforceRelationTargetExposure`.
2. **No-protocol host, addressed object (E3).** After #36337, a host with no protocol service refuses the relation condition but may still serve a disabled package's object when it is addressed directly through the `query` fallback. Measure it first.
3. **Declaration (S2).** #36337 added the root export `objectPackageDisabledError` to `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, so ITS declaration reads `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. The PR body and the claim were corrected by the seat; its changeset `.changeset/35526-calldata-relation-disabled-package.md` still reads `no (narrowing…)`. If that changeset has not been consumed by a release when this card's PR lands, correct its `Clause-②:` line to `yes (narrowing…)` in the same commit that fixes its N5 sentence (it glosses a system context as "a hook's `ctx.api`", which never passes through `callData`) and narrows its TO line to "a condition directly beneath a lookup of the queried object". If it has been consumed, say so in this card's PR body and correct the CHANGELOG entry instead. This PR declares its own Clause-② truthfully as well.

## To do

1. Measure items 1 and 2: a two-hop member pin per door, and a directly-addressed object on a no-protocol host.
2. Descend every hop the engine serves, for both the package question and the exposure question, on `callData` and the stdio bridge.
3. Pin the refusal order (disabled before unexposed), a condition under `$or` / `$not`, and the "re-enabled" control that actually disables and then re-enables (N1, N3, N4).

This is a narrowing on a published door, so its L2 runs on the narrowing face at the contract-review tier.

## Note

The system-caller half (whether a system context is refused too) is a separate maintainer decision on #35526. If it is ruled B, its PR can take this card's items in the same change.

Blocked-by: #36337

## Grade
p1 · area:package · domain:server (same inference as #35526, which the maintainer graded p1: field values from 1 / 0 answers after a disable, one relationship further). A disabled package's data stays readable to a member through a two-hop condition.
